title: Console onboarding: add Marketplace entrypoint + improved error/retry UX
creator: Chris Osei
description:
## Context
Marketplace customers (AWS/GCP) are hitting avoidable friction immediately after subscription: they land in the standard console onboarding, don’t know they need to “link” a marketplace entitlement, and when entitlement propagation is delayed they see generic errors with no actionable next steps.

This ticket adds a marketplace-specific entrypoint into console onboarding with:
- a dedicated “Connect your Marketplace subscription” step
- explicit error states for common entitlement failures
- retry guidance + self-serve troubleshooting links
- lightweight instrumentation hooks (full analytics eventing is tracked in ENG-22114)

Primary success metric (tracked at the program level): reduce median time-to-first-token for marketplace buyers; locally, reduce onboarding abandonment at “org provisioning / entitlement validation”.

## Goals
1) Provide a clean entrypoint for users coming from AWS/GCP Marketplace (Launch / Configure / Manage Subscription → Redwood Console).
2) Make entitlement validation failures actionable (what happened, what to do next, how long to wait, when to contact support).
3) Support “existing Redwood org” linking as a first-class path.
4) Ensure the UI works for both AWS + GCP with minimal provider-specific branching.

## Non-goals
- Implementing entitlement verification endpoints (ENG-22110).
- Hardening entitlement sync / background job reliability (ENG-22116).
- Full funnel analytics spec and dashboards (ENG-22114) — we will add basic event hooks and stable identifiers.

## UX / Flow
### Entry points
A) Marketplace deep-link (preferred)
- Console route: `/onboarding/marketplace`
- Query params supported:
  - `provider=aws|gcp`
  - `subscription_id` (where available)
  - `product_code` / `offer_id` (where available)
  - `account_id` (optional; for display only)
- If params are missing, user can still proceed and we show a manual “Lookup entitlement” path.

B) In-console entry
- Console banner shown to newly-created users who have no API key + no usage + no active entitlement but arrived with `utm_source=aws_marketplace|gcp_marketplace`.
- CTA takes them to `/onboarding/marketplace`.

### Screens
1) “Connect your Marketplace subscription”
- Explains what will happen:
  - Verify the subscription
  - Link to a Redwood org
  - Provision initial limits + billing association
  - Create first API key
- Primary CTA: “Verify subscription”
- Secondary CTA: “I don’t have a subscription” (links to docs / listing)

2) “Choose organization”
- If user belongs to 0 orgs: create new org (default)
- If user belongs to 1+ orgs: select org OR create new
- Copy callout: linking affects billing/limits for that org

3) Verification + linking (async state)
- Calls entitlement verification endpoint (ENG-22110) and then links entitlement to org.
- Shows spinner with sub-steps (“Verifying subscription”, “Linking to org”, “Preparing your workspace”).

4) Success
- Shows: org name, provider (AWS/GCP), entitlement identifier (short form), next steps
- CTA: “Create API key” (goes to standard API key create flow)
- CTA: “View Marketplace billing” (if available; otherwise links to docs)

## Error states (must be explicit)
All error states include:
- human-friendly summary
- what to check
- when to retry
- “Retry verification” button
- “Contact support” button with prefilled debug details (provider, entitlement/subscription id, org id, request id)

### Error taxonomy (UI mapping)
1) `ENTITLEMENT_NOT_FOUND`
- Message: “We can’t find this subscription yet.”
- Guidance: entitlement may take 5–15 minutes to propagate; confirm correct cloud account / project; confirm subscription is Active.

2) `ENTITLEMENT_PENDING`
- Message: “Your subscription is still being activated.”
- Guidance: wait and retry; we display “Last checked: <timestamp>”.

3) `ENTITLEMENT_ALREADY_LINKED`
- Message: “This subscription is already linked to another Redwood organization.”
- Guidance: switch org, or contact support to verify ownership; do NOT offer self-serve unlink.

4) `ORG_PERMISSION_DENIED`
- Message: “You don’t have permission to link subscriptions to this org.”
- Guidance: ask an org admin/owner; show required role.

5) `PROVIDER_AUTH_FAILED` (rare; mostly for backend)
- Message: “We couldn’t validate with your cloud provider.”
- Guidance: retry; if persists contact support.

6) Unknown / fallback
- Message: “Something went wrong while verifying your subscription.”
- Guidance: retry; share request id.

## Engineering requirements
- Add a new onboarding route + state machine entry for marketplace.
- Preserve the ability to complete normal onboarding if marketplace flow fails (escape hatch).
- Ensure idempotency: repeated retries must not create duplicate orgs or duplicate linking attempts.
- Display a stable `request_id` / correlation id from backend responses when present.
- Add telemetry hooks (non-blocking):
  - `console_marketplace_onboarding_viewed`
  - `console_marketplace_verify_clicked`
  - `console_marketplace_verify_succeeded`
  - `console_marketplace_verify_failed` (include error code)
  - `console_marketplace_retry_clicked`

## Implementation notes
- Frontend feature flag: `marketplace_onboarding_entrypoint` (on in staging; gradual prod rollout).
- API contract:
  - `POST /v1/marketplace/entitlements/verify` (ENG-22110)
  - `POST /v1/marketplace/entitlements/link` (existing internal endpoint; ensure error codes are mapped)
- Provider-specific labels only affect copy and which identifier we show (AWS subscription vs GCP entitlement).

## Acceptance criteria
- User can complete the entire flow (marketplace → console → org linked → API key created) in staging.
- Each of the error taxonomy cases above has a dedicated UI state (no generic toast-only failures).
- Retry guidance is visible and actionable for `NOT_FOUND` and `PENDING`.
- “Contact support” includes debug payload in the support modal / mailto (provider, org id if selected, subscription id if present, request id).
- No regressions to standard onboarding.

## Testing plan
- Unit tests: route parsing (provider/ids), state transitions, error mapping.
- Integration test (staging):
  - happy path with seeded entitlement
  - `NOT_FOUND` (fake id) → retry
  - `ALREADY_LINKED` with test entitlement
- Manual QA checklist (Design + QA):
  - copy/layout for long ids
  - mobile/responsive
  - accessibility: focus management and screen-reader label on error blocks

## Rollout
- Stage 1: staging only, flag on.
- Stage 2: prod flag on for internal accounts only (Redwood email domain).
- Stage 3: prod gradual to 10% of marketplace-tagged traffic.
- Stage 4: 100% + remove legacy marketplace workaround banner.
